body: Tested locally, it works as expected on Compatibility. This is a great start, but I think we can push further on usability, especially for less programmer-centric workflows such as VFX. **Testing project:** [test_pr_105701.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21640832/test_pr_105701.zip) *Press K to toggle real-time texture updates to compare performance.* https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d721cad-a0e9-4065-81c2-24d00f8ce6c0 *Original shader: [Colorful Bubbles](https://www.shadertoy.com/view/4d3BWH) by JuliaPoo* Some feedback: - It currently doesn't work on Forward+/Mobile, but this is expected given what's said in OP. - It took me a long time to figure out how you associate the shader with the DrawableTexture resource. I originally expected there would be a ShaderrMaterial property on the DrawableTexture, where you could assign a material (with its uniforms) and its shader. - The width/height, format and mipmaps could be set directly as properties on the DrawableTexture inspector. Combine this with a property to set an array of base textures and a ShaderMaterial, and you wouldn't need any script for basic usage. More advanced usage (e.g. blitting over an area that isn't the whole texture size) would still warrant a script, but the use case for creating procedural textures would be simplified a lot. - I think we can provide this high-level functionality and keep low-level behavior intact, but we need to make sure it's not initializing textures twice in this case (e.g. by reading inspector properties then the user's own `start()` call). - Additionally, there is no quick way to just use a plain background color to blit over the entire area to apply your own shader. Some procedural textures initialize/update asynchronously, so using GradientTexture2D won't work unless you `await get_tree().process_frame`, which is not possible if you attach the script directly to the DrawableTexture2D like I originally did (since it's a Resource and can't access SceneTree directly). I ended up attaching the script to a node instead so I could use `_process()`, but I figured it was worth mentioning nonetheless. The testing project also includes a pure black `black.png` image for this purpose. - Having a DrawableTexture already set on a material property won't update it if you call `start()` to initialize it. You need to set it in a script again after calling `start()` for it to be recognized: ```gdscript drawable_texture.setup(64, 64, DrawableTexture2D.DRAWABLE_FORMAT_RGBA8, true) drawable_texture.blit_rect(Rect2(0, 0, 64, 64), preload("res://white.png"), Color.WHITE, 0, preload("res://drawable_texture_material.tres")) material_override.albedo_texture = drawable_texture # This line is required for the texture to appear, even if we loaded it in the inspector previously. ``` If you update the texture in real-time, you also need the last line to be in `_process()`, which is more resource-intensive than it could be. - Passing `null` as a texture parameter in `blit_rect()` causes a crash: ``` handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11 Engine version: Godot Engine v4.5.beta.custom_build (faf3a2d29b8775eb2354e339d353b03869041aa0) Dumping the backtrace. shaders go for different numbering as per the [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/sky_shader.html#global-built-ins): > There are 4 `LIGHTX` lights, accessed as `LIGHT0`, `LIGHT1`, `LIGHT2`, and `LIGHT3`. I'd go for `COLOR0`/`COLOR1`/`COLOR2`/`COLOR3` for consistency. - DrawableTexture should get its own icon, so it can look different from Texture2D (which is an abstract class, and therefore has a gray icon): For future PRs: - `TIME` is not accessible in `texture_blit` shaders, but I think it should to make procedural effects easier. You can emulate it for now by passing a `time` uniform manually in `_process()`, then calling `setup()` every frame. - Having this as a built-in implementation would also need an update mode property in DrawableTexture, which would control when to update the texture: **Automatic** (always update only if `TIME` is used), **Once**, **Always**.

@ColinSORourke @clayjohn OK, code wise I think this all looks good, nothing stands out to me that needs touching up. The only thing really is that the `linear_to_srgb` conversion is an all or nothing deal. In the sample project that I made it's important that only SOURCE0 is converted. However by setting the correct format I think it worked correctly anyway.

So I created a sample project, a very bare bones texture painter that paints albedo/normal/ao/roughness and metallic. It all worked very well and did exactly what it should do.
You can find the resulting demo project here: https://github.com/BastiaanOlij/drawable-textures-demo

I also streamed developing this, it's a 2 hour watch but might help provide some more context: https://www.youtube.com/live/O1gwSoXTv_g

There is room for improvement but the things I ran into can all be follow up things, the heart of this is solid and I'm for merging the implementation as is.
The things I think we should consider for the future are:
- I missed the ability to set a default color for the content. White is not a good default for a normal map or ORM texture :)
- I know Reduz was adamant around the `setup` function and doing everything in code, but working with it I feel it makes far more sense to make these properties of the texture.
- The aforementioned issues with wanting more control/certainty about linear output v.s. sRGB output.
Just some nitpicks and a rebase needed, then let's merge for 4.7 dev1!

Looks great! Thank you so much for your persistence, this has been a huge amount of work, but the results are looking great. Let's get this merged in dev1 so we can get lots of feedback prior to stable!!!
